sources.title: Raise Rectification Request FAQs | Income Tax Department
sources.snippet:
Ans. A request for rectification can be submitted on the e-Filing portal if there is any mistake apparent from record, in an Intimation issued u/s 143(1) or in an order u/s 154 passed by the CPC or in an Assessment Order passed by the Assessing Officer.   
 In respect of the rectification request against the order / intimation passed by CPC, the taxpayer needs to select “Rectification of orders passed by CPC. [...] Q10.     Can I rectify my previously filed ITR using the rectification request service?  
 Ans.    If you notice a mistake in your submitted ITR, and it has not been processed by CP

verdict.one_line: This is a genuine Section 143(1) intimation from the Income Tax CPC Bengaluru for ₹4,820 due by 13 November 2026 — you can pay it or file a rectification request yourself on the e-filing portal.
verdict.why: The notice is verified as REAL_LIKELY with a valid DIN and no scam signals. Section 143(1) intimations are automated summary assessments for arithmetical or apparent errors; they do not involve income verification. The taxpayer can either pay the demand via e-Pay Tax or submit a rectification request under Section 154 on the e-filing portal if there is a mistake apparent from record.

timeline.what_happens: Notice is available in your e-Proceedings account; review the computation and decide whether to pay or seek rectification.
Pay the ₹4,820 through the e-Pay Tax facility or file a rectification request under Section 154 on the e-filing portal to correct any apparent mistake.
Last date to respond; if nothing is done, the demand becomes final and interest under Section 220(2) may start accruing.
Unpaid demand attracts interest at 1% per month (or part thereof) under Section 220(2); the department may initiate recovery proceedings.
Continued non-payment can lead to a notice of demand under Section 156 and further recovery action such as attachment of bank accounts or refund adjustment.

action.reply_draft:
Subject: Response to Section 143(1) Intimation for AY 2025-26 – [Your PAN]

Dear Sir/Madam,

I refer to the intimation under Section 143(1) of the Income Tax Act, 1961 received via e-Proceedings dated [date you saw it], demanding ₹4,820 for AY 2025-26.

[If paying:] I have made the payment of ₹4,820 through the e-Pay Tax facility on the e-filing portal on [date]. The challan details are: BSR Code: [______], Date: [______], Challan No: [______].

[If filing rectification:] I believe there is a mistake apparent from record and hereby submit a rectification request under Section 154. The details of the alleged error are: [briefly state the error, e.g., mismatch in TDS credit, incorrect deduction claimed, etc.]. Supporting documents are attached.

I request you to kindly update the records accordingly.

Thank you,

[Your Full Name]
[Your PAN]
[Your Address]
[Your Mobile Number]
[Your Email]
Date: [Today’s Date]

Details of the alleged error (if filing rectification)

Challan copy (if paying via e-Pay Tax)
